fields.description:
Sibling of cabc-7a98-d173-4d7c, found in its Phase-1 sibling sweep (E5). Jira DC's shared pager
`_paged_search` loops on `startAt` offsets with no stall guard. A server that ignores/repeats
`startAt` (returns the same page) spins forever — measured: 26 calls to the experiment harness cap
— instead of terminating loudly. Same defect class as cabc (Cloud acli_graph cursor spin, fixed by
ab7f in 30c522cde9) and `fetcher._iter_pages` (guarded since bug deac).

CORRECTED LOCATION: the original description cited `adapters/jira/transport.py:379-416`. Ticket
465d's one-module-per-capability split has since landed and moved the pager verbatim to
`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/_base.py:120-157` (`_TransportBase`,
the shared pager every capability mixin inherits).

## Proven root cause (runtime-confirmed; full RCA in the ticket comments)

M1 — `_base.py:141-157`: the pager's ONLY loop exit is `if not batch: break`. `start_at` advances
locally but nothing verifies the SERVER honoured it, so an offset-blind instance re-serves the same
non-empty page forever and the exit is unreachable (`out` grows unbounded). Runtime evidence: a
`startAt`-ignoring stub drove 26 calls, requesting offsets [0,3,6,9,12,15,18,21,24,27,...] while
receiving page 1 every time; terminated only by the harness cap.

M2 — `_hierarchy.py:91`: `get_parent_map` wraps the drain in a bare
`except Exception: warn; return {}` degradation contract, which converts any pager-level abort into
a SILENT empty parent map. Runtime evidence: the same stub returned `{}` after 26 calls, raising
nothing. So M1's loud signal is neutralised at this caller unless re-raised ahead of the broad clause.

Legitimacy = defect, against cited authority: `fetcher.py:336-344` (the same operation on a
parallel surface raises `SilentTruncationError(reason="offset-stall")`, contract stated at
`fetcher.py:275-277`), `acli_graph.py:29-46, 79-86` (the Cloud sibling raises
`RunawayPaginationError` and its readers re-raise past fail-open at `acli_graph.py:304-306`), and
the prior CLOSED `Fixed:` bug cabc for this same class.

## Plan

Scope is deliberately narrow — ticket 465d owns re-architecting the DC transport modules and
another stream owns `set_parent`/parent handling — but the EDIT SET IS NOT ONE RE-RAISE. Plan
review (T4/T5b/G1G2) correctly found that `_paged_search` feeds THREE whole-project readers and
that ALL THREE are consumed by `fetcher.fetch_snapshot` behind broad `except Exception` fail-open
handlers (`fetcher.py:610` parent, `fetcher.py:652` comment, `fetcher.py:688` issuelink). VERIFIED:
`fetcher.py` names neither stall error (grep for `RunawayPagination` there returns nothing), so a
stall raised in the transport is swallowed at the fetcher boundary and the pass writes a silently
degraded snapshot. A guard that stops at the transport boundary would therefore NOT resolve the
original report. There are FOUR fail-open sites to pierce, not one.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE ERROR TYPE (also plan-review advisory A1: do not mint a third bespoke error for
one class). `fetcher.py` is CORE and must be able to name the error, but core must never import
adapters — verified: `fetcher.py` imports nothing from `adapters/`, while adapters already import
`BackendEnvError`/`BackendHTTPError` FROM core (`_links.py:19`, `transport.py:66`). So the error
belongs in core's `_backend.py` beside the other `Backend*` errors, where both the DC adapter and
`fetcher` can name it with no layering inversion — one canonical type for the class rather than a
third bespoke one.

1. `_backend.py` — add `BackendPaginationStallError(RuntimeError)` beside the existing `Backend*`
   errors (`_backend.py:38-60`). Docstring states the invariant: a paged whole-project read whose
   server stopped advancing is a TRUNCATED read, and readers must re-raise it past their fail-open
   handlers rather than degrade around it.
2. `_base.py` — in `_paged_search`, remember the previous page's first issue key; if a page repeats
   it, raise `BackendPaginationStallError`. The server is not honouring `startAt`, so paging can
   never advance. Fires on the SECOND call.
   DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE from `fetcher.py:335-345`: fetcher returns cleanly (no raise) when the
   repeated page is SHORT, reasoning a client that returns fewer items than asked and then repeats
   "has nothing further to give". That does NOT transfer to DC. This pager exists (bug 9263)
   precisely because a hardened DC caps EVERY page below the requested size via
   `jira.search.views.default.max` — so on DC a short page is the NORMAL case WITH more to give, and
   adopting fetcher's short-page branch would silently return 20 of 250: the exact 92%-loss defect
   this pager was built to refuse. `_paged_search` therefore raises on ANY repeated page, short or
   full. It cannot false-positive: a `startAt`-honouring server serves DIFFERENT issues per offset.
3. `_hierarchy.py` — add `except BackendPaginationStallError: raise` immediately ahead of
   `get_parent_map`'s broad `except Exception` (`_hierarchy.py:91`), mirroring `acli_graph.py:304-306`.
4. `fetcher.py` — add `except BackendPaginationStallError: raise` ahead of each of the three broad
   `except Exception` enrichment handlers (`fetcher.py:610`, `:652`, `:688`). This is the boundary
   that decides whether the whole pass fails loudly or writes a degraded snapshot, and a stall must
   fail loudly: consumer confirmed — `fetch_snapshot`'s caller is the reconciler pass, which has no
   `{}`-specific expectation for these enrichments (each is guarded by `hasattr` and merges only
   what it gets), so the propagated error aborts the pass with the transport's own
   `_call_logged` WARNING already emitted (`_base.py:60-66`) plus the raised message — instrumented,
   not an uninstrumented traceback.
5. `transport.py` — re-export `BackendPaginationStallError` through the existing `__all__` facade
   (2 lines; no other change to that file, which 465d owns).
6. Tests — the RED oracle (see Verification).

NOT IN SCOPE, ticket to be filed and linked `discovered_from`: Cloud's own
`acli_graph.RunawayPaginationError` is swallowed by these SAME three fetcher handlers, so bug cabc's
fix (commit 30c522cde9) is itself incomplete at the fetcher boundary. Making Cloud stalls propagate
is a behaviour change on the Cloud surface owned by another stream, so it is filed rather than
folded in here.

## Verification

RED→GREEN with the oracle held out from the implementing subagent, plus a defect-seeded mutation
check (re-remove the guard -> the test must return RED). Oracle lives in
`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_dc_transport_pagination_heldout.py` and covers: a
`startAt`-ignoring stub proving loud self-termination within 2 calls; the error escaping
`get_parent_map`'s fail-open; the error escaping all three `fetch_snapshot` enrichment handlers;
the facade import; and the unchanged 250/250 recovery for well-behaved page-capping servers through
all three whole-project readers. Then `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the DC + fetcher +
acli_graph pagination suites.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `_paged_search` raises a dedicated runaway/stall error when `startAt` does not advance
- [x] Fail-open exception handling does not swallow the stall error at ANY of the four sites: the
      transport's own `get_parent_map`, and all three `fetcher.fetch_snapshot` enrichment handlers
- [x] Held-out test with a `startAt`-ignoring stub proves termination within 2 calls
- [x] The stall error is re-exported and importable through the `transport.py` facade
- [x] Existing DC pagination behaviour for well-behaved servers unchanged (250/250 still recovered
      from a page-capping client through all three whole-project readers), and the pre-existing
      `get_parent_map` fail-open contract still returns `{}` for ORDINARY failures
